{{< include _head.qmd >}}

Tchaikovsky wrote his harmony textbook in 1871 from his lectures at the Moscow Conservatory; Jurgenson published it in 1872, and
in English in 1900. These are its modulation examples: each starts in C major and reaches another key, near or far, in a few chords. They
are grouped by the book's example number.

How to read the labels and use the scores: [Analysed Scores](index.qmd#reading-the-labels). For modulation itself, see
[Chapter 22](../modulation.qmd).

{{< include _tchaikovsky-harmony.qmd >}}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## For teachers

- **Source:** the notes and analyses are the DDMAL Key Modulation Dataset's encodings of the book's examples (Néstor Nápoles López and
  others), translated automatically to RomanText and copied into When in Rome. `scripts/when-in-rome/build.mjs` reads the MusicXML
  (`src/tchaikovsky`), and every note was checked against music21's reading of the same files.
- **Example 185a** uses `im7`, a minor seventh chord on the tonic of the new key; it is shown as written.
- **Not edited:** the analyses are an automated translation and are shown as they are.
:::
